title: Logarithmic corrections to bulk and surface criticality in a three-dimensional quantum Heisenberg antiferromagnet
authors: Xuyang Liang, Xiao-Chuan Wu, Zenan Liu, Zhe Wang, Zheng Yan, Dao-Xin Yao
abstract: At the bulk upper critical dimension, marginally irrelevant interactions generate multiplicative logarithmic corrections to mean-field scaling. While these corrections are well understood for bulk observables, their consequences for boundary criticality, particularly for finite-size scaling, remain much less explored. Here we combine large-scale quantum Monte Carlo simulations with boundary renormalization-group analysis to study a (3 + 1)D O(3) quantum critical point. After verifying the known logarithmically modified bulk finite-size scaling, including the correlation-length scaling governed by the logarithmic finite-size exponent \hat{\coppa}, we tune the surface coupling to identify ordinary, special, and extraordinary boundary regimes. For the ordinary and special transitions, we derive logarithmic correction exponents and \hat{\coppa}-dependent finite-size scaling forms for boundary correlations, including results that have not been systematically established before. These predictions are quantitatively supported by Monte Carlo data. In the extraordinary regime, we find long-range surface magnetic order and a logarithmically enhanced surface-bulk correlation.
summary: This paper rigorously examines the impact of logarithmic corrections on the critical behavior of a 3D quantum Heisenberg antiferromagnet at its surface. By combining large-scale Quantum Monte Carlo simulations with Boundary Renormalization Group theory, the authors characterize three distinct boundary regimes (ordinary, special, extraordinary). The work provides new theoretical predictions and quantitative numerical evidence for how these logarithmic terms govern finite-size scaling near the quantum critical point.
main_problem: The study investigates how logarithmic corrections modify critical behavior at both the bulk and surface levels of a quantum antiferromagnet near its upper critical dimension.
main_result: The authors derive new, quantitatively supported logarithmic correction exponents for boundary correlations in ordinary and special transition regimes, while also confirming long-range surface order in the extraordinary regime.
method: The research combines large-scale Quantum Monte Carlo (QMC) simulations with rigorous Boundary Renormalization Group (RG) analysis to analyze finite-size scaling.
model_or_system: The system is a spin-1/2 columnar-dimerized quantum Heisenberg antiferromagnet realizing a (3+1)D O(3) quantum critical point. The Hamiltonian includes bulk and surface coupling terms ($J_1, J_2, J_s$).
key_observables: Bulk staggered moment ($\langle M_z^q angle$), surface staggered moment ($\langle M_z^{q,s} angle$), susceptibility ($\chi(q)$), correlation length ($\xi$), and the surface Binder ratio ($R_2$).
important_parameters: The analysis distinguishes between three critical regimes based on the surface coupling $J_s$: ordinary, special, and extraordinary transitions.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on extending known mean-field results to include multiplicative logarithmic corrections in finite-size scaling forms.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the lattice structure (Fig 1), show bulk observables confirming expected logarithmic scaling at the QCP (Fig 2), and plot the surface Binder ratio ($R_2$) vs. $J_s$ to map out the different critical regimes (Fig 3).
paper_structure: The paper first establishes the theoretical framework for logarithmic corrections in the bulk, then uses QMC simulations to verify these effects. It proceeds by analyzing the surface criticality across three distinct regimes—ordinary, special, and extraordinary—deriving specific scaling forms and exponents for each.
why_interesting: The detailed study of boundary critical phenomena, especially incorporating higher-order logarithmic corrections beyond mean-field theory, provides crucial insights into how dimensionality reduction or boundaries modify fundamental quantum phase transitions relevant to strongly correlated materials.
